narrative.what_i_did:
This was a quarterback session driving the DynastyTrust x Tapit Phase 1 integration across both repos at once. The operator opened both repos, said he wants them to work together, and told me to quarterback the whole thing; when I surfaced a chip-form question about where to point the first batch he chose all of Phase 1 together (the Nostr signing bridge, sign-in by attestation, and the education-bot slice). I grounded hard before cutting: I read the cross-repo build map and the quarterback workflow, the Tapit-side integration cut-list brief, the previous session.json, and -- crucially -- I diffed the two vendored tapit-attest copies and read the real signing surfaces in both apps. That grounding changed the plan in three important ways, all captured in the new DynastyTrust doc docs/integration-phase1-signin-and-bridge.md.

The Tapit education cut (TW-1) shipped this session. I added a new src/features/education/ feature: literacy.ts (a typed LessonContent catalog with eight concepts, reusing the existing secretLiteracy strings by reference so there is one source of truth), ExplainChip.tsx (a reusable progressive-disclosure inline explainer that reveals consequence then why-it-works then the-crypto on successive taps), a jargon-guard test, and a manifest registered in features-registry.ts. No existing screens were touched -- ExplainChip is not mounted anywhere yet, that is a later cut. All four Tapit gates are green (typecheck, lint, 791 tests including the new ones, build). Commit 4e6403c, [skip ci], on the working branch, not pushed to main.

On the DynastyTrust side a sibling agent shipped DT-2 (rungs 0-9 curriculum plus the Express/Rabbit-Hole dial) as commit 96c5256, building on the assistant scaffold that already existed there. I audited both delegated cuts myself before pushing: the Tapit education code has zero key/sign/secret references, and DynastyTrust's bot still holds the SAFE-context allowlist with no key material ever entering the prompt. I also wrote and committed the Phase 1 integration plan in DynastyTrust as a resume marker (4062380).
narrative.whats_pending:
Two of the four Phase 1 cuts remain, both documented precisely in DynastyTrust docs/integration-phase1-signin-and-bridge.md. Cut A is sign-in by attestation: the primitive already exists here in tapit-attest/src/core/sign-in.ts (buildSignInChallenge / answerSignInChallenge / verifySignIn), so the remaining work is a new Tapit sign-request intent 'sign-in' that answers a challenge and returns the attestation in the grant, plus DynastyTrust's verify path, two netlify functions, and a session-minting flow. It is lower risk because it never touches a spend.

Cut B is the signing bridge and it is the money-touching one. The honest finding is that signing a vault PSBT is not signing an attestation -- Tapit's sign-request flow only knows attest/cosign-existing over attestation envelopes, and the BIP341 tapscript machinery (parsePsbt, serializePsbt, tapLeafHash, tapscriptSighash, the /0/0 derivation) lives only in DynastyTrust's psbt-signer.ts because tapit-attest is deliberately zero-Bitcoin-script. So the bridge requires porting that signer into Tapit and proving byte-for-byte parity with a cross-repo test BEFORE any sat rides on it. I deliberately did NOT rush a hand-rolled BIP341 signer this session; that would violate safe-beats-fast and the rule that an attestation is never a spend signature. The plan stages it B0 (shared signer + parity test, the gate), B1 (new psbt-cosign intent + meaning-banner), B2 (DynastyTrust requester + absorb), B3 (multi-member over the Nostr inbox).
narrative.what_you_could_do_better: Nothing surfaced beyond the declared scope. One judgment worth recording: I delegated both education cuts to parallel agents (one per repo) rather than cutting them myself, which was the right call for non-money UI/content work and kept my quarterback context clean for the money-touching grounding, but it means the next session should still give ExplainChip a real mount point and field-test the Dynasty dial on device -- the cuts are correct and gate-green but not yet exercised by a human. The other honest note is that 'all of Phase 1 as one batch' is genuinely more than one session of safe work once the bridge's parity discipline is respected; I shipped the two safe cuts and turned the two hard cuts into a grounded, staged plan rather than pretending to finish them.
narrative.bigger_picture: The whole integration thesis lives or dies on one wall: an attestation expresses intent and can never move a coin, while a tapscript signature moves a coin and is never an attestation. This session put the two safe, intent-side cuts (education in both apps) on the board and drew the dangerous, coin-side cut (the signing bridge) as a staged plan whose first step is a parity test, not a feature. That ordering is the doctrine made concrete -- the education layer teaches the user the very wall that the engineering must never cross, and the bridge only earns build time once a byte-parity test proves Tapit signs exactly what DynastyTrust would. Tapit's role in the larger map is clear and unchanged: it is the one place the keys live and the place the ceremonies run, and DynastyTrust is the place the Bitcoin script is compiled and enforced. Phase 1 is the wiring that lets a person log into the vault app with their sovereign identity and, eventually, sign a vault spend from the wallet that holds their keys -- without ever handing those keys to anyone.

next_session_starts_with: Two Phase 1 cuts shipped (education in both repos). Two remain, both fully specced in DynastyTrust docs/integration-phase1-signin-and-bridge.md. START with Cut A (sign-in by attestation) because it is lower risk and the primitive already exists in tapit-attest/src/core/sign-in.ts: add a new Tapit sign-request intent 'sign-in' in src/features/sign-request/* that calls answerSignInChallenge and returns the SignInAttestation in the grant, then wire DynastyTrust's Auth.tsx + two netlify functions (challenge issue, verify+mint-session) + a users_tapit_keys migration. THEN do Cut B0 -- the BIP341 signer byte-parity test between DynastyTrust's psbt-signer.ts and a Tapit port -- and do not ship any psbt-cosign UI until that test is green. Also give ExplainChip (shipped this session) a real mount point at a high-value decision screen and field-test the Dynasty Express/Rabbit-Hole dial on the iPhone. Nothing merges to main until the operator gives the explicit batch-merge go.
feedback_to_appcommander: The cross-repo quarterback pattern worked well here: one orchestrating session holding both repos' maps, fanning out per-repo agents for the independent non-money cuts, and reserving the money-touching crypto for grounded design rather than delegation. Two reinforcements worth lifting. First, when a primitive is claimed 'NEW' in a build map, verify against the actual vendored code before cutting -- sign-in.ts already existed in Tapit's tapit-attest, and the DynastyTrust education bot was already scaffolded, so a chunk of Phase 1 was further along than the map implied. Second, the divergence between the two tapit-attest copies (0.1.0 vs 0.1.1-wallet.0, different internal helpers) is a standing hazard for any shared-digest or shared-signer work; the doctrine note should be 'never assume the two vendored copies agree -- prove it with a parity fixture,' which is exactly the gate the signing bridge now hangs on.
